Geometries and vocabulary labels; free text comes back as placeholders.

post.description:
Body: the plugin source as a tarball. Our worker rebuilds, hashes and signs it; that
bundle (not the sandbox's) is what gets registered.
The sample's fingerprint if we have one, else a `fingerprint` job to poll.

get.description: A synthetic fixture's bytes (made from the fingerprint alone), for the build sandbox.
Job summary (counts, state, error classes) and, for boundary jobs, the typed result.

Worker-computed checks (de-identification). Sessions need `versioning.checks`; the
worker itself posts through /api/v1/worker/versioning/checks with its worker token.

get.description: The Studio setup (`.studio/`: lockfile, environments, READMEs) at a branch, oid or `tag:<release>`.

get.description: This run's events from the outbox (same polling as the project stream).

post.description:
A tarball of a plugin package → checks, and unless `dryRun`, a signed, content-addressed
`generated` registry entry with a provenance attestation (§9; todo10 Phase 3). `runId`,
`promptHash`, `model` and `sampleDigests` go into the attestation.

A tar of an OCI image layout (`oras copy --to-oci-layout`, or GET …/export) → verified,
stored and registered in this workspace at `tier`. A person's action: `plugins.approve`.
Approve or reject (`{"decision": "approve" | "reject", "reason"}`); a second person only.

get.description: README and skills, fetched lazily by agents (§8.2). Plugin-authored text: callers treat it as untrusted.

The stored artifact as a tar of an OCI image layout (manifest tagged `<version>`, plus
its signature and attestation referrers), ready for `oras copy -r --from-oci-layout`.

Fetch-and-hash for the browser (todo10 Phase 3): the sha256 of every file in the package
and the bytes of the `include`d ones (comma-separated paths; the manifest's
`ui.contributions` is always included). The browser hashes the bytes,
checks them against `hashes`, and recomputes the tree digest from `hashes`; it must equal
the digest the workspace pinned. Verified here too, on this load.

post.description:
Ask for the next tier (generated → organisation → curated). People who manage plugins
ask (agent sessions aren't allow-listed for it, kernel/agent_scope.py); a second person approves.
The simple form (pick folders, pick a preset); the guided path is confirming a proposal.

get.description:
What the dataset holds and how it is shaped (docs/datasets.md §11.1): collections, fields,
formats, relationships and issues, from inspection. Counts and technical facts only.

Server-sent events for a project. The stream reads the outbox (the same table every
replica writes), so it works behind any replica and keeps nothing in process memory; the
browser reconnects after `SSE_MAX_S` with `Last-Event-ID`, and invalidates its queries.

post.description:
A folder or a selection as one ZIP, streamed (stored entries, constant memory). Entry
names are current paths, never the names files arrived with. Files held for privacy
review are left out and listed in `_held_files.txt`.

get.description:
The whole queue, filtered by type, severity and dataset; `facets` counts the unfiltered
queue for the filter controls. The Overview's attention block is its first five rows.

post.description: The broker: a plugin's use token + an outbound request → the provider's response.
A workspace user mints a narrower session token (e.g. for an agent run). Scopes can only shrink.

Only a person, with a reason; recorded in the audit log (this is a development check,
not de-identification).

get.description:
One version's bytes (D6), named `name (v1).ext` unless it's the current one. Audited like
a download; refused while the file, or that version, is held for privacy review.

The task document's items, a page at a time (todo11 D8): with `item.*` events, the
Studio inserts and upgrades items instead of refetching the document.

post.description: The items on screen: workers process them first (a hint; the latest one wins).

get.description:
Whether the Studio should use versioned saves: the service is configured (and, best
effort, reachable). The web reads this to switch its save path on.

post.description:
`resourceClasses`: the pools this worker runs (default cpu, memory); `heartbeat: true`
means it renews the lease through the progress call, so it gets the short lease.
The heartbeat. 409 means stop: the lease was lost or the job was cancelled.
A worker that is shutting down (SIGTERM) hands its job back to the queue.

todo13 D13: the name-screening backfill, a slice at a time (every worker asks about once a
minute; each call works at most `budgetS` seconds, paced by API_NAME_SCREEN_QPS). Resumable:
it always takes what is still unscreened. Concurrent calls only share the work.
The archive stays a File, flagged with why it wasn't unpacked (the chip shows it).
Run a read or report-check versioning operation in a workspace, as the worker.

get.description: What the active plugins in this workspace can do: one row per capability, summaries only.
